description:
The published-curve dataset records digitization precision in log10 decades while the campaign acceptance predicate applies it as a linear BER offset.

## Background

The reference dataset documents per-point digitization precision delta as a width in log10 space. The campaign comparison accepts a published value p when p lies in [L-delta, U+delta] with delta applied linearly. For the current eBCH(128,64) grid the interpretations disagree only where delta is nonzero (the 1.55 dB order-2 point and the order-1 series), and no acceptance verdict changes under either reading; the defect is the silent unit mismatch, not a current wrong verdict.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The acceptance predicate and the dataset agree on one documented unit for digitization precision, converted explicitly at the comparison boundary.
- [hard] REQ-02: A test exercises a nonzero precision value and pins the agreed interpretation.
- [hard] REQ-03: The dataset provenance note and the campaign receipt name the same unit.
title: digitization precision units differ between dataset and acceptance predicate
